svg.title: A question, end to end
svg.desc: Eleven steps. The browser posts the form; Vercel's edge gives the request its id; the middleware binds it to every line; the form is checked; the turn starts, logging only the question's length, and makes its first event before the response; the agent calls Gemini at most five times; each tool call is checked and runs on the question's lane, the cache first; the events go back as they happen; the browser puts each in its place and keeps the conversation for the next question; the lines say how it went; and once it has answered, the lines go to Axiom and any error to Sentry, while LangSmith gets the run with its words hidden.
svg.text: A question, end to end
"Will it rain in Paris tomorrow?", from the form to the answer and its lines
The browser posts the form
htmx sends the question, the conversation so far, the browser's language and time zone, and the lane
Vercel's edge
HTTPS; the request's id, its own; the firewall's rules, once set; then the function, in Washington, D.C.
The middleware
binds the id to every line the request logs, puts it on the response (x-request-id), and adds the security headers
The form, checked
256 KiB, 10 fields, each once; the question 1 to 2,000 characters; the conversation 10 messages at most; a broken rule gets our sentence
The turn starts
chat.request logs the question's length, never its words; the system prompt, the conversation, the question; a deadline; the first event, made first
The agent, and Gemini
at most 5 calls, 20 s each, the first words within 10 s; Gemini asks for tools, the graph runs them; the last call has no tools, so it ends in words
A tool call, on the question's lane
its input checked, 8 s; the cache, then Open-Meteo; or our own MCP server; or Apify's Actor, falling back to its twin if it fails
The events go back as they happen
each chip as its call starts and ends; each piece of the words; then the finished answer, its Markdown made HTML that can only be text and links
The browser
htmx puts each event in its place; the conversation, this answer with it, waits in the form for the next question
The lines
each tool call; each request out, or cache hit; how the answer ended, with its tokens and time; the request, its status; never the question
Once it has answered
Vercel keeps the function alive (wait_until): the lines to Axiom, any error to Sentry, within 2 s; LangSmith has the run, its words hidden
The question is never logged, traced or kept on our side: Gemini gets it; every other service gets less.
Open-Meteo: a place's name, a point rounded to about 1 km · Apify: the rounded point · the logs: a length, ids, times, classes
